flawed_step: Line 0785 assumes a decomposition T_pE ≃ T_πE ⊕ T_{\bar π}E without assuming that p splits in the CM field. The subsequent construction of generators a,b and the quotients \overline L_n relies on this decomposition.
counterexample: Take K=Q, E:y^2=x^3-x, and p=3. The curve has CM by Z[i] and good reduction at 3 (its discriminant is 64), while p splits completely in K trivially. But 3 is inert in Q(i), so Q(i)⊗Q_3=Q_3(i) is a field, not Q_3⊕Q_3. Consequently T_3E has no decomposition over Q_3 into distinct π- and \bar π-parts as asserted in line 0785.
assessment_summary: The proof of case (3) uses an ordinary/split-CM decomposition that fails for an allowed good prime. The explicit CM elliptic curve at p=3 therefore invalidates a necessary step of the proof.
